action.rationale: Fresh run with dim=10 and budget=100 (< 20·dim=200), so a light probe (P1–P3) is recommended to learn global structure without overspending; probe evaluations feed the archive.

Probes indicate weak global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.112, top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.94) and a small overall budget (100 ≈ 10·dim), so we should hedge between a global population method and a model-based method. A short race (18 evals ≈ 18% of budget) will identify which adapts faster before we commit the remainder.

CMA-ES won the race decisively (57.4M vs 83.98M in 9 evals) and hasn’t run a full round yet (evals_in_tenure=0, sigma=2.87, not converged). Probes indicate weak global structure (P2 fdc=0.112, top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.94), favoring a population method over immediate local polish. With 70 evals left, one CMA-ES round now should improve further and still leave ~20 evals for final polishing.

Only 20 evaluations remain (out of 100), so we should refine rather than explore. BOBYQA needs 2·dim+1 = 21 evaluations to start in 10-D, which exceeds the remaining budget, while CMA-ES has stalled for 13 evals with sigma still 2.62. Polishing the incumbent (3.792e7) with L-BFGS-B is the fastest viable local option now.
